body:
OBSERVED FLAKY 2026-08-19, on Windows CI, and measured in both directions before blaming anything.

THE FAILURE, on PR #439 — a branch whose ONLY change was adding JSON to
scripts/rail-renames.json, which cannot reach a renderer:

    AssertionError: expected [ 500, 503 ] to deeply equal [ 200, 503 ]
    AssertionError: expected [ +0, +0, 1, +0 ] to deeply equal [ 1, +0, +0, +0 ]
    AssertionError: expected 'the renderer could not start' to contain 'root'

BOTH DIRECTIONS:
- main is GREEN on the identical code (d20608f9, the tip that branch was cut from).
- ubuntu-latest passed on the same commit; only windows-latest failed.
- RE-RUN of the same job on the same commit PASSED.

So it is a Windows-runner flake in the spawn-budget rails, not a defect in the diff.

WHY IT FLAKES, from the rail's own header (test/gateway/render-spawn-clock.test.ts): "spawn alone
cost ~0.8s at load 200 on 16 cores, against a 500ms budget". The rail pins a spawn WINDOW, and a
GitHub Windows runner is slower and narrower than the machine those numbers came from. Under load the
worker does not reach `online` inside the window, so the door answers 500 and the rail reads it as a
refusal it did not expect.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN SHRUGGED OFF: the re-run passing is exactly the moment the habit forms.
A test that is sometimes red trains whoever sees red to re-run instead of investigate, and that
deletes the value of red — which is the whole argument of T187, one rail over. Observing it and
moving on would be the same mistake in a different file.

THE FIX MUST NOT BE A WIDER SPAWN BUDGET. That budget is the subject of the rail: T139 split the
spawn clock from the render clock precisely so a loaded host stops refusing healthy renders, and
widening the number under test would assert whatever the machine happens to do. The honest options
are to make the rail's timing independent of wall-clock (inject the clock, as the render-window half
may already do), or to give the spawn window a floor derived from the machine rather than a constant.

CONSTRAINT: test/gateway/render-spawn-clock.test.ts is T139's rail and T139 is archived, so it is
FROZEN. Changing it needs the two-PR authorization dance (scripts/rail-renames.json on the base
first), and only if the change is expressible as substitutions — which a clock injection is not.
That makes this Myk's call, not a repair I can land.

RAILS: whatever lands must fail when a spawn genuinely exceeds its budget, proven by forcing it —
the same proof T187's fix carries.
title: The spawn-budget rails flake on Windows CI — a timing fixture on a slower runner
